Thanks — ran a quick sketch (high level, back-of-envelope) based on GreenLeaf’s 80–120M token window and peak profile. Attaching the sheet with scenarios — sending the headline here so we can iterate: 

Headline pricing (hosted API, includes KV prefix caching assumptions and standard 99.9% uptime SLA):
- On-demand (no commit): $600 per 1M tokens — recommended only for short POC due to cost.
- 12-month commit bands (monthly commit, billed monthly):
  * 0–99M / month commit: $520 per 1M tokens
  * 100–199M / month commit: $400 per 1M tokens
  * 200M+ / month commit: $300 per 1M tokens

Recommendation for GreenLeaf (given stated 80–120M): propose the 100M commit band (on-contract at $400/1M) with a 10% overage cap at commit price for the first 20% burst, and an overage rate of on-demand for anything beyond. If they sign a 12-month upfront/annual commit we can move the 100–199M band to $365/1M.

Burst policy (proposal):
- Allow 2.5x sustained peak TPS for up to 30 minutes per day and up to 40 hours per month cumulative without charging above commit price (counts against burst allowance).
- Longer bursts billed at overage rate (on-demand).

Unit economics note: at 100M tokens/month with $400/1M GC, revenue runs ~$40k/month — we should expect GPU-backed hosted costs + caching efficiencies to give us margin at that level assuming moderate sequence lengths (avg token length ~25 tokens per request). If their average tokens per call are significantly higher, we’ll revisit.

Next steps from here:
- Vanessa: send this sketch to Asha with the 100M commit recommendation and include the mutual action plan + procurement checklist.
- Marissa: confirm whether we can offer the additional annual-pay discount to $365/1M and flag any mandatory terms to escalate.

If GreenLeaf is comfortable, we can offer a short pilot month at the 100M commit price with retrospective true-up while they validate traffic.
